claims.text: Large language models are prone to hallucination by generating plausible yet nonfactual content.
Hallucination raises significant concerns over the reliability of LLMs in real-world information retrieval systems.
LLM hallucinations present distinct challenges that diverge from prior task-specific models due to the open-ended general-purpose attributes of LLMs.

evidence.description: LLMs are prone to hallucination, generating plausible yet nonfactual content.
This phenomenon raises significant concerns over the reliability of LLMs in real-world information retrieval (IR) systems...
Given the open-ended general-purpose attributes inherent to LLMs, LLM hallucinations present distinct challenges that diverge from prior task-specific models.

methodologies.name: Taxonomy of LLM Hallucinations
methodologies.description: A comprehensive categorization framework for hallucination types, contributing factors, detection methods, benchmarks, and mitigation techniques in LLMs.

limitations.text: Retrieval-augmented LLMs face current limitations in combating hallucinations in information retrieval systems.

future_work.text: Investigating hallucination in large vision-language models.
